description:
auth.rs:62-64:

    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct CustomCaTransport {
        der_cert: Vec<u8>,
    }

A DER-encoded CA certificate is not a private key, so this is not a credential-leak in the strict sense — but it is deployment-identifying material. The byte sequence uniquely identifies the deployment's PKI: its Subject DN, public key, signing algorithm, validity window, and any X.509 extensions. In federated/multi-tenant scenarios, leaking the byte sequence in logs reveals which private-CA-using customer the client is configured to talk to.

The derived Debug prints the full Vec<u8>, which for a typical 2048-bit RSA CA cert is around 1 KB of base16-like hex output — actionable to a log-reader who can decode it.

Workspace pattern (auth.rs:183-188 for BearerAuth, 233-238 for BasicAuth, request.rs:212-227 for Session) handles similar cases with manual redacting Debug. CustomCaTransport is the outlier.

Severity: low. The DER bytes are not a credential. The risk profile is 'a sysadmin tailing application logs learns which deployment this client is configured for', which is fine in most cases but matters in compartmentalised multi-tenant setups.

Fix: manual Debug impl that prints CustomCaTransport { der_cert: <NN bytes> } where NN is der_cert.len(). One-line change, matches the cookie-cutter pattern of the other Debug-redacting types in this file.
title: CustomCaTransport.der_cert derives Debug, prints raw byte vector for deployment-identifying material
